initial_prompt: I just found out my dad has cancer. I don't know what to do. Everything feels overwhelming.

messages.content: I just found out my dad has cancer. I don't know what to do. Everything feels overwhelming.

I'm really sorry you're going through this. Finding out a parent has cancer is shocking and it's completely natural to feel overwhelmed right now.

A few thoughts that might help:

**Let yourself feel what you're feeling** - There's no "right" way to react. Scared, numb, angry, sad - all of it is okay.

**You don't have to figure everything out right now** - Take things one step at a time. Today might just be about absorbing the news.

**Ask questions when you're ready** - What type of cancer, what stage, what's the treatment plan? Information can help reduce some of the scary unknowns, but get it at your own pace.

**You can be there without having all the answers** - Sometimes just being present with your dad matters more than saying the perfect thing.

**Take care of yourself too** - You can't pour from an empty cup. It's not selfish to eat, sleep, and do things that help you cope.

Is there anything specific that feels most pressing right now - practical things you need to figure out, or do you just need to process this emotionally? I'm here to listen either way.
